description: Breastfed by a she-wolf, founders of Rome… and fratricides. A myth that places law and boundaries before blood.

hero.hook: Rome was not born from a soft pact. She was born from a she-wolf, a sacred furrow... and a killed brother.

blocks.text: The story of **Romulus** and **Rémus** is the founding myth of Rome. This is not a children's story. It's the story of a double rupture: a  who breaks her vow of chastity, then a **fratricidal** who places the law before blood. [[vestal virgin]]
Roman tradition does not hide this crime. It makes it the basis of a city built on the sacred border and the survival of the State, more than on the family.

In Alba the Long, city of the descendants of Aeneas, the usurper **Amulius** hunts his brother Numitor. To extinguish the lineage, he forces his niece **Rhea Silvia** to become a vestal. But **March**, god of war, unites with her. Twins are born.

blocks.caption: Mars and Rhea Silvia: the divine birth of twins.

blocks.text: Amulius orders them to be drowned in the Tiber. The flooded river deposits the cradle near the **Palatine**, under the fig tree . A **she-wolf** breastfeeds them; a woodpecker, bird of Mars, feeds them. The shepherd Faustulus and his wife Acca Larentia raise them. [[Ficus Ruminalis]]

blocks.caption: The Capitoline she-wolf, image of orphaned and predatory Rome.

blocks.text: In Latin, “lupa” means she-wolf… and prostitute. Ancient authors already suggested that Acca Larentia, nicknamed as such, was the true “wolf” of the legend.

As adults, the twins overthrow Amulius and restore Numitor. Then they want to found their own city. Romulus chooses the **Palatine**; Remus, the Aventine. To decide, they take the : Remus sees six vultures first; Romulus next sees twelve. [[omens]]

blocks.caption: The Palatine: the hill where Romulus traces Rome.

blocks.text: Romulus traces the , the sacred furrow of the enclosure, and promises death to anyone who crosses it. Remus jumps over, in defiance. Romulus (or his lieutenant Celer) kills him. Rome was founded on April 21, 753 BC. , year I of the  calendar. [[pomoerium]] [[Ab Urbe Condita (753 BC)]]
April 21 remains the “Natale di Roma”. At midday, the sun hits the entrance to the Pantheon: an effect that ancient architects would have designed to magnify power.

First problem: the city lacks women. Romulus organizes games and invites the neighbors. In the middle of the party, the Romans kidnap the young girls: the **Rapt of the Sabines**. The **Sabins**, led by Titus Tatius, declare war.

On the battlefield, Sabine women, already mothers of Roman children, intervened between fathers and husbands. The war stops. The two peoples merge. Romulus and Titus Tatius rule together. The Romans took the name . Rome becomes a society that integrates the enemy. [[Quirites]]

After thirty-seven years of reign and the creation of a Senate of one hundred "fathers", Romulus disappeared during a storm on the Champ de Mars. The official version says that Mars takes him to heaven: he becomes the god **Quirinus**. Another version whispers that the senators assassinated him.
The image of  remains: an orphan city, nourished by savagery, capable of transforming marginalized people into masters of the world. [[The Capitoline Wolf]]

blocks.text: Founded on fratricide and kidnapping, Rome draws from its myth a clear idea: the survival of the State and respect for the sacred border come before blood ties.
